seoDescription: A decade inside Fortune 500 delivery taught us that the engineering is rarely what slows a project down. AgenticDraft exists to fix the rest of it — and then to leave.

hero.heading: We spent a decade inside Fortune 500 delivery.
hero.headingAccent: We left to fix the part nobody bills for.
hero.lede:
The code was rarely the problem. Getting a decision made was the problem. Finding out why something had been built that way was the problem. Discovering that the one person who understood it had left in March was the problem.
We started AgenticDraft because we got tired of watching capable teams lose to their own process.

chapters.title: Enterprise platforms, and the processes behind them
chapters.body:
Consulting for Fortune 500 companies, mostly on Adobe Experience Manager and Edge Delivery Services, with React and Angular front ends on top. Enterprise web platforms, content systems, design-to-code pipelines, automated delivery. The design-to-code pipeline we built on that work took 60–70% out of the time between a design and production code.
Then the half of the work that never touches a browser: eight years inside a regulated financial-services business — billing and invoicing logic, debt-collection workflows, national-registry integrations, and seven production automations built and documented end to end on UiPath. Later, multi-agent orchestration across those same processes, which cut time-to-information by more than 40%.

chapters.title: The bottleneck was never technical
chapters.body: It was the approval chain with eleven names on it. The architecture decision that lived in one person's head. The handover that turned out to be a calendar invite and a link to a repository. Work that should have taken a fortnight took a quarter, everyone involved could see it happening, and nobody was in a position to stop it.

chapters.title: The expertise and the overhead were being sold together
chapters.body: That is the part that finally got us. The knowledge was worth what clients paid for it. The machinery wrapped around the knowledge was not — and it was the larger of the two invoices. So we left to find out what the first thing looks like without the second.

chapters.title: We build ourselves out of a job
chapters.body:
Most consultancies are structured to stay: the longer an engagement runs, the better it goes for them. We are structured to leave. Every engagement ends with workflows your own team runs without us, documentation written for somebody who has never seen the system, and a codebase a new starter can learn from in their first week.
Staying on afterwards is on the table, and plenty of teams want it. The difference is that by then it is a choice rather than a dependency.

chapters.title: Fortune 500 practice, without the Fortune 500 invoice
chapters.body: Enterprise standards are not expensive to apply. They are expensive to discover — and that discovery has already been paid for. What we charge reflects the work rather than the logo on the case study, which is how a company with a modest budget ends up running the same pipeline as one with a nine-figure programme behind it.

pullQuote:
If you still need us in a year, we got something wrong.
If you still want us, we got it right.

closing.heading: Bring us in early,
closing.headingAccent: and keep us because you want to.
